title: Finite column expansion of a total element
statement:
For a ring R, theorem total_resolution_element_finite_support
    (K : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] (n : ℤ)
    (h_positive : ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero (K.X p))
    (z : (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ x : ∀ i : ℕ, (K.X (-(i : ℤ))).X (n + (i : ℤ)),
      z = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r + 1),
        K.ιTotalOrZero (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (-(i : ℤ)) (n + (i : ℤ)) n (x i)

proof.text: Let M_i = K^(-i,n+i) for i in the natural numbers and let f from the dependent finite-support sum of the M_i to Tot(K)^n be the linear sum of their inclusions, constructed with DFinsupp.lsum. To prove f is epi, suppose f followed by g equals f followed by h. Test this equation on DFinsupp.single i a: DFinsupp.lsum_single gives equality after the inclusion of M_i. Every summand K^(p,q) with p+q=n and p<=0 has this form, with i=(-p).toNat and q=n+i. The other summands are zero: the degree-q evaluation functor maps h_positive to IsZero K^(p,q), so equality after their inclusions is automatic. HomologicalComplex₂.total.hom_ext therefore gives g=h. ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective provides a finite-support vector x mapping to the given z. Take r to be Finset.sup id of x.support (zero for empty support). Each supported i satisfies i<=r. DFinsupp.lsum_apply_apply and DFinsupp.sumAddHom_apply express f(x) as the support sum. DFinsupp.sum_of_support_subset extends it to Finset.range (r+1), because each inclusion maps zero to zero. This proves the required expansion with coordinates x i, without a cycle condition or horizontal exactness.
